name: 1801 Indiana Avenue — Stone-front brick dwelling (district draft; refined by T-1946)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), 40 ft, the north end of a row of four (1801-1807) behind a stone (blue) strip run along their Indiana fronts; a 1-storey brick store (S) built forward of it to the street line'. Carried to 1904 on the T-3151 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3151, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1946 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 27w trace (s27wfp-indiana_1801-b1), the T-3151 census (s27w-1801-front, s27w-1801-stores) and the T-1837 register row frontage-27w-1801 (Stone-front brick dwelling); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-background-3151).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-3151 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1801 S. Indiana Avenue, parcel indiana_1801 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Indiana Avenue, the background behind Prairie Avenue: Indiana Avenue's east frontage, 18th to 20th Street, and East Eighteenth Street's row at 213-217 (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 27).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 14.000, v -2.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet is tied to sheets 20 and 28 where it meets them (T-3150): 0.67 m RMS over its six control components, with no independent check of its own, plus about a pixel (0.05 m) of trace. derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front), widened to 5.5 m along the front because the fitted strip was narrower than any house of the avenue (T-2690). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s27wfp-indiana_1801-b1 p3 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 70% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'Stone-front' overlaid with the frontage row: A background house with no named record and no register row: the brick family's hip over the sheet's printed storeys, every face closed, nothing read beyond the sheet. 3B, the north end of the row of four (1801-1807) behind the stone strip the sheet runs along their Indiana fronts; the one-storey store built forward to the street line and the two stores on 18th Street at 205-207 are 1911 shops whose 1904 state is not read, so they are kept out of the draft (`keep_out`: the store's band 0-4.4 m from the street line, short of the stone strip, and the stores' band from the house's rear wall, 16.9 m, back to the lot's rear). Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 83810314 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-district-background-3151.
